articles.title: Quote of the day by Neem Karoli Baba: “God will give you everything you need for your spiritual development. Hold on to nothing.”; What Maharaj ji advices on having faith in God and leaving attachment to material possessions
articles.description: Today success is often measured by what we own, how much we earn, or how many achievements we collect. We spend years only running after our set ambitions, bigger goals, better identities, and popularity believing that happiness is based upon how much more we have.Yet, despite all the progress, there is still that feeling of unsatisfaction, restlessness, frustration and being a miss lingering at the back of people’s mind. This inner emptiness often arises because while our outer lives keep expanding, our inner lives remain neglected.But Neem Karoli Baba, also known as Maharaj ji, gives us a different perspective. He tells us that true fulfillment does not come from accumulating possessions, status, or even certainty. Instead, it comes from learning to develop trust, inner peace, and a deeper connection with something greater than ourselves.

articles.title: ABP LIVE Doc Talk | Is Your Weight Causing Your Back Pain? Here's What Experts Say
articles.description:
Being obese has become an increasingly common medical problem around the globe, and many people of different ages suffer from this condition. It is known that overweight people are prone to developing diseases like diabetes and cardiovascular issues; however, obesity significantly influences spinal health as well. The burden of extra body fat imposes extra pressure on the spine, muscles, and joints, resulting in back pain. Learning about the effects of excess weight on back pain is important in order to prevent this painful issue.

Effects Of Obesity On The Spine

Spine serves as a support for body weight while being flexible enough to move. In case of overweight or obesity, additional pressure appears to be placed on the spine, especially in the lumbar region. The spinal discs serve as pads between the bones of the spine and due to excessive pressure, they may experience compression and develop inflammation leading to back pain.

When individuals are obese, their center of gravity becomes positioned in front of their bodies, meaning that they need to correct it with the help of shifting their spine. As a consequence, they suffer from developing bad posture, additional curvature of their lower backs, and unbalanced muscles. Due to increased workload on the muscles, individuals become fatigued and stiffened.

Low Levels Of Mobility And Muscular Strength

The level of physical activity among obese people is low since they do not feel comfortable enough performing their usual exercises. As a consequence, muscles in their backs and cores become weaker, thus being unable to protect the spine from injuries, which results in chronic pain and lack of flexibility.

How Maintaining Ideal Body Weight Helps To Reduce The Pain

One of the best methods of reducing back pain is maintaining an ideal body weight through eating a well-balanced diet and performing physical exercises regularly. Individuals should start with low impact sports such as walking, swimming, cycling, and yoga in order to improve flexibility and posture. It has been clearly established that there is a direct link between obesity and backaches. Obesity leads to extra pressure being exerted on the spine, causes poor postures, weakens the muscles that provide support, and speeds up the deterioration of the spine. Through adopting healthy lifestyles that include good diets, exercises, and weight control, one can minimize his or her risks of having back pains.
